description: The line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC, in percentage) of five different methods—Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, and ROME—across varying co-occurrence numbers, with the x-axis representing the co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale ranging from 1 to 1000, and the y-axis showing accuracy from 30% to 55%. The Base method, represented by black circles connected by a solid line, starts at approximately 28% accuracy and shows a slight increase to around 32% as the co-occurrence number increases. The FT method, shown with blue downward triangles and a solid line, begins at about 32% and rises gradually to roughly 38%. The MEMIT method, indicated by purple diamonds and a solid line, starts at approximately 35% and increases to about 46%. The MEND method, marked by brown squares and a solid line, starts at around 36% and rises to approximately 45%. The ROME method, represented by green squares and a solid line, starts at about 44% and shows a steady increase to nearly 57%. All methods exhibit an upward trend in accuracy as the co-occurrence number increases, with ROME consistently achieving the highest accuracy across all values of the co-occurrence number.
